title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not part of Grothendieck's motivic Galois notes. It is page 16 of a typed Bourbaki document (header 'n° 505'), scanned upside down and filed among the motives manuscripts. It is a list of corrections and insertions to a draft of Bourbaki's Topologie générale, chap. IX, §6 (Polish, Suslin and Lusin spaces). The references to 'P. 129' and 'P. 130' fit that chapter's page numbering. Its contents, in modern terms:
(1) In two statements on p.129, the hypothesis 'metrizable' is weakened to 'Hausdorff' (séparé).
(2) A corrected proof that I=[0,1] is the image of a zero-dimensional ('éparpillé') Polish space under a continuous bijection. Take the dyadic map f:{0,1}^N→I, (ε_n)↦Σ ε_n 2^{-n}, which is continuous and surjective. Let D be the countable set of nonzero sequences with finitely many nonzero terms. Removing D keeps, for each dyadic rational, only its expansion ending in 1's; the zero sequence keeps 0. Then P={0,1}^N−D is a G_δ in Cantor space, hence Polish and zero-dimensional, and f|P is a continuous bijection onto I. This is the step showing that every Lusin space is the continuous bijective image of a zero-dimensional Polish space.
(3) New corollary. A countable topological sum of Lusin spaces is Lusin. A countable projective limit of Lusin spaces is Lusin, because it is a closed subspace of a countable product of Hausdorff spaces, and countable products of Lusin spaces are Lusin (proof of prop. 11).
(4) A starred remark: the distribution spaces D'(Ω), E'(Ω), etc. with the strong topology are Lusin spaces.
(5) Further local corrections: a topology defined as the projective limit of discrete topologies on sets C_n; 'fermées' replaced by 'ouvertes'; a closure condition on the sets φ_{n+1}(c') in a Suslin/Lusin-scheme construction.
The surrounding pages of the folder (gerbes, motivic Galois groups, G^{(0)}=G_m×G') are unrelated to this sheet.
errors: With summation from n=0 the map Σ ε_n 2^{-n} has image [0,2], not I=[0,1]; the weight should be 2^{-n-1}, or the sum should start at n=1. Likely a slip in the typescript.
Minor point: 'dyadic expansion' is ambiguous at dyadic rationals; the removal of D implicitly selects the expansion ending in 1's. This is correct but left implicit.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a misfiled Bourbaki redaction sheet (corrections to TG IX §6 on Lusin spaces), and all its content is standard and published. The only mild archival interest is its presence in Grothendieck's motives folder.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down; the transcription correctly reads it rotated.
'I' is the interval [0,1]; underlining in the original marks the modified words ('séparé', 'bijection', 'limite projective', 'ouvertes', etc.).
